claims.text: No allergen or cross-contamination information is published by the shop. Kitchen size (approximately 6 tsubo total) means separation may be limited.
Soy sauce is not used in kakigori preparation, so wheat-via-shoyu is not a relevant risk for this format.
Condensed milk and whipped cream are used in several items and prepared in the same small counter kitchen; dairy cross-contact cannot be ruled out for fruit-only orders.
No information on staff allergy-awareness training or handling protocols has been published. The shop has not advertised any allergen accommodation service.
Shaved ice with pure fruit syrup (no dairy topping) is a simple, naturally wheat-free preparation that avoids most common gluten sources.
All syrups are prepared without heat (non-heated raw syrup) from fresh fruit, with no mention of added thickeners or wheat-containing stabilizers.
「卵・乳製品・小麦を持ち込まない」 — eggs, dairy, and wheat are never brought into the workshop, eliminating wheat-flour cross-contact at source.
「当店のお菓子は全てグルテンフリーです」 — every product in the shop is gluten-free.
Sweets bakery — no soy sauce used; base ingredients are rice flour, soy milk, sugar, rapeseed oil, almonds, aluminum-free baking powder.
No egg, dairy, or butter used anywhere; soy milk and rapeseed oil replace animal products. Honey status per-item unconfirmed given the shop name 'Miel'.
Staff conduct allergy intake interviews (アレルギーの聞き取り) and make custom products, including soy-free, on consultation.
Founded specifically to serve children with food allergies so they can eat safely alongside everyone.
Dedicated wheat-free facility with an explicit no-wheat-on-premises policy.
No dedicated-fryer or celiac cross-contact protocol is stated on any source; the karaage wrap implies frying, and shared oil/surfaces cannot be ruled out — confirm on site.
Owner is a wheat-trained (Germany/France) pastry chef and Hakodate Pilsner (barley) beer is poured on premises, so gluten is present in the building even if the food menu is rice-flour based.
One local blog describes the bagel as 国産小麦100% (100% domestic wheat), conflicting with the owner-sourced keizai.biz 国産有機米粉100% (rice flour) — verify the bagel flour in person.
Co-located dog trimming salon is walled off from the cafe and involves no food, so it does not add wheat cross-contact to meals.
The 照り焼き (teriyaki) wrap option almost certainly uses wheat-containing soy sauce unless tamari is used — unconfirmed; ask before ordering.
Not a vegan kitchen; dairy, egg and meat handled alongside plant items. No sourced vegan cross-contact information.
No sourced description of allergy handling or celiac accommodation beyond the general gluten-free-conscious concept.
Self-branded gluten-free × organic × additive-free cafe with a food menu built on 国産有機米粉100% rice flour and enzyme brown rice — inherently wheat-free ingredients.
Owner personally trained in patisserie/cooking abroad for ~8 years and set the cafe's stated goal of making gluten-free an everyday choice.

Shared (not dedicated GF) kitchen; samosa / keema-samosa on the menu use traditionally wheat-flour pastry, so wheat is present on premises and cross-contact is possible — celiac guests should avoid the samosa and confirm plating.
Curries use a 15-spice house blend; commercial garam-masala / curry-powder blends are occasionally cut with wheat flour, so the specific blend should be confirmed wheat-free on the day.

No soy sauce is mentioned in the curry recipes; South-Asian-style spice curry typically uses none, but this is not explicitly confirmed — ask whether any しょうゆ/soy sauce is used and, if so, whether it is tamari.
Mains are chicken/keema/egg based and desserts/lassi are dairy; plant sides are not confirmed animal-free, so vegans must ask.

The shop actively advertises its curries as gluten-free / grain-free and butter-free, indicating awareness of wheat-avoidance, but no formal allergen protocol or dedicated-kitchen claim is documented.
Official site: 「グレインフリーのカレーをご堪能下さい」— enjoy our grain-free curry.
KissPress review: 「同店のカレーは全てグルテンフリー」— all of the shop's curries are gluten-free.
Budou-chan: curries are 【グルテンフリー】【バター不使用】(gluten-free, butter-free).
A kids' curry (キッズカレー) is offered, making the shop family/child-friendly.

name: Retreat Field (リトリートフィールド · 姫路こころの事業団)

claims.text: 小規模な就労施設の製造・直売所。米粉製品専用ラインか小麦と共用かは未確認。要確認。
季節のプリンは卵・乳を含む可能性。ぽりっと・米粉麺は植物性。
『自然栽培農法で育てたお米や、その米粉を使った米粉麺』を販売。米粉麺は小麦アレルギーの人でも食べられるとする。
自然栽培米100%の米粉を使ったグルテンフリーの菓子・乾燥麺。ぽりっとは授産品コンクール銅賞。
斎麺(ラーメン)の麺にグルテンフリー表記なし=通常小麦麺の想定。焼き菓子(いぶき製)は8大アレルゲンフリーだが提供環境は要確認。
店内でクラフトビール(Free Spirits Brewing／大麦)を提供。
完全ヴィーガン。動物性原材料・乳製品・精製糖・うまみ調味料・アルコール調味料は不使用。
『動物性原材料不使用且つ8大アレルゲンフリーだけでなく、着色料や添加物も不使用で安心・安全の商品』としてヴィーガン菓子を販売。
ドーナツ・クッキー・マドレーヌ・レモンケーキ・スノーボールは動物性不使用＋8大アレルゲンフリー(小麦不使用・米粉)。

name: Motomachi Satonaka Himeji (元町サトナカ 姫路店)

claims.text: Shared kitchen: the chicken katsu curry and chicken-cutlet topping are panko-breaded and fried, and the Himeji branch also serves keema curry pasta and cheese curry doria — all wheat items cooked in the same space as the wheat-free curries, so cross-contact is possible.
The shop's claim is specifically that the curries use no wheat flour ('すべてのカレーが小麦粉不使用'), not that the whole kitchen is gluten-free; no dedicated GF prep line or fryer is mentioned in any source.

No Japanese source mentions soy sauce (醤油) or tamari in the curry; the base is described as an additive-free dashi of kombu, shiitake and chicken bones, so the curry sauce itself appears free of soy sauce.
Caveat: the 半熟味付玉子 (seasoned soft-boiled egg) topping is a marinated egg that in Japan is typically steeped in a soy-sauce-based liquid (soy sauce usually contains wheat) — confirm before adding it.
Every curry contains chicken and a chicken-bone dashi, so vegan diners are limited to vegetable sides (pickles, potato sabzi); no vegan curry exists.
The shop markets its curry to allergy sufferers ('アレルギー持ちの人も安心'), indicating allergy awareness, but no source describes a specific cross-contact protocol for the shared kitchen.
Every curry sauce is genuinely made without wheat flour ('無添加・無化調・小麦粉不使用グルテンフリーのスパイスチキンカレー'); thickening comes from an 8-spice blend and dashi, not roux.
Additive-free, no chemical seasonings, with a mild kid-friendly chicken curry over turmeric rice — a workable safe meal for a celiac child if ordered plain.

name: Saka no Ue no Ureshinaru (坂の上の嬉しなる)

claims.text: オーダーメイドで中身は変幻自在。グルテンフリーは選択肢の一つで、生麩仕立て等小麦を使うケーキもある小規模共用キッチン。
『くるみ醤油』を使う和スイーツあり=小麦醤油の可能性。要確認。
生クリーム・チョコの組合せもあり、卵乳との共用環境。
スポンジは全て米粉で卵・乳・小麦不使用、アレルギー対応ケーキを提供。オーダーメイド可。
米粉スポンジのグルテンフリーケーキを常設・オーダーメイド対応。
